subject: plastic water bottle
title: What If You Only Drank Bottled Water?

scenes.text: What if you only drank bottled water? You'd be drinking something nobody could count until 2024.
Columbia University scientists aimed lasers at bottled water to spot plastic far too small for older methods.
They found about two hundred forty thousand plastic particles in an average litre.
Nine in ten were nanoplastics, up to a hundred times more than earlier estimates.
Particles that small can get past the gut and into blood and organs, and their effects are still being studied.
A single litre held a quarter of a million of them, likely shed by the bottle and the water filters.

description:
What if you only drank bottled water? A 2024 study in PNAS from Columbia University used laser-based imaging to count tiny plastic particles in bottled water from three brands: about 240,000 per litre on average, around 90% of them nanoplastics.
That is 10 to 100 times more than earlier estimates. Nanoplastics can pass into the blood and organs; health effects are still being researched.
